buyer.rubric: The buyer is the Chief Revenue Officer, Chief Growth Officer, CMO, Chief Product Officer, Head of Growth, Head of Product, Head of Business Development, or the Founder or CEO at a company under about 50 people. Compliance officers, MLROs, heads of risk, general counsel and CISOs are never the buyer.

seller.competitorTest: A competitor sells vendor-agnostic identity-verification, KYC or age-assurance infrastructure into compliance, risk, legal and MLRO functions who need regulatory defensibility, not into growth or product teams optimizing signup conversion.

description: Ondato sells identity verification and age assurance as a conversion product: 97% pass rate, 30-second onboarding. It sells to privately held consumer fintechs, neobanks, payments and PSPs, lending, trading, crypto, and age-gated platforms that run high-volume self-serve signup in the UK, Ireland, the US or Canada, with $2M to $250M raised or $1M to $150M revenue. Public companies, larger groups, verification vendors, consultancies, agencies and non-profits are out. The buyer owns the signup funnel and is measured on conversion; compliance roles are never the buyer. A dated situation is a bonus for the message, never a condition: a new market or licence, a consumer product launch needing signup verification, a funding round in the last 120 days, users complaining about stuck verification, or age-assurance exposure under the UK Online Safety Act or US state laws.

requirements.text: The company is headquartered in, or serves consumers or SMBs in, the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States or Canada.

The company runs a high-volume consumer or SMB self-serve signup in fintech, neobanking, payments, lending, trading, crypto or an age-gated consumer platform. A company that serves only businesses through sales-led onboarding, or whose record shows no self-serve signup, does not qualify.
The company is not a verification vendor, a compliance consultancy, an agency or a non-profit.
The company is privately held with $2M to $250M raised or $1M to $150M revenue. A record with neither figure, a public company, or one above the band does not qualify.

Within the last 12 months: a new market entry or licence; a consumer product launch that needs signup verification; a funding round in the last 120 days; users complaining about stuck verification; or an age-assurance statement under the UK Online Safety Act or a US state law.
